reviews.reasoning: Independent re-derivation first, ruling second. NUMBERING: Ps 150 is an identity psalm - ps_lib.web_to_mt(150,v) returns (150,v) for v=1..6 with mt_to_web the exact inverse, and verse_map_web.json carries no Ps.150.0 title pseudo-ref (psalm_device_inventory.json superscriptions has no entry for 150), so no dual-cite arithmetic and no title-evidence question arises on this row. Tool baseline re-run on the row: citation_sweep.py GREEN (ref validity, X-X span form, per-psalm dual-cite arithmetic, witness disclosure, cross-tradition guard), check_refs_mirror.py GREEN (web:Ps.149.4 and web:Ps.149.5 are the only out-of-span verses argued and both sit in boundary_evidence_refs), check_web_quotes.py GREEN on 3 curly-quoted WEB strings, check_marks.py GREEN (pmarks_Ps.json records no selah, no ketiv/qere, no reversed nun and no suspended letter anywhere in Ps 150; the single paseq logged at Ps.150.1 is seg-layer and the row makes no paseq claim), check_language_zones.py GREEN, check_tiling.py 6/6 verses over Ps.150.1-Ps.150.6 with 0 gaps and 0 overlaps, check_universals.py 2 FLAGS. TIER-1 FRAME: confirmed against the inventory rather than assumed - Ps.150.1 is listed under halleluyah.verse_initial and Ps.150.6 under halleluyah.verse_final, and the same initial/final pairing holds for each of Ps.146-150, so the five-psalm bracket in device_notes is byte-supported discussion texture rather than received lore. IMPERATIVE CENSUS re-derived, not trusted: a per-token scan of MT Ps.150.1-150.6 from verse_map_oshb.json returns hallelu-initial tokens 3/2/2/2/2/1 at MT 150:1,2,3,4,5,6 = 12 tokens across 6 verses, exactly the row's figure, and its 2-anchor/10-interior split is right (the anchors being MT 150:1 token 0 and MT 150:6 token 4). DOXOLOGY-FORMULA SWEEP re-derived: skeleton ברוך (spliced from oshb:Ps.41.14, skeleton tier) occurs in 0 verses of Ps 150 and 16 verses book-wide, and skeleton אמן (spliced from oshb:Ps.41.14, skeleton tier) in 0 verses of Ps 150 and 5 verses book-wide, while book_boundary_doxologies records baruch at all four seams oshb:Ps.41.14, oshb:Ps.72.18-oshb:Ps.72.19, oshb:Ps.89.53 and oshb:Ps.106.48 with amen counts 2, 2, 2 and 1 respectively - so the row's rejection of the coda rival on shared-formula grounds is a textual argument with a digit-bearing sweep behind it rather than taste. INSTRUMENT ROSTER: the count of 8 is auditable because the row enumerates its members, and it correctly keeps the waw-prefixed dance token at MT 150:4 (skeleton ומחול, spliced from oshb:Ps.150.4) out of an instrument/sound census; WEB names the same eight across web:Ps.150.3-web:Ps.150.5. SPAN: I support it. The one internal seam candidate is 150:5|150:6, and the bytes bind it shut rather than open it - the verse-final hallelu-Yah at MT 150:6 is the closing member of an inclusio whose opening member stands at MT 150:1, a device straddling the candidate seam, and a 6-verse psalm sits squarely inside the short-indivisible whole_psalm rule. WARRANT: three OL defects, one of them factual. The row's principal Hebrew citation is not quotation-grade (nfd, not byte); its register claim is contradicted by the pointed bytes of the very verse it quotes and by its own imperative count in the same field; and its Hebrew quote and the gloss beside it do not cover the same span. None of the three moves the span, so this is a challenge to the warrant and to a factual claim with the span left standing, and confidence high stays defensible for the span once the false register leg is removed, because the inclusio carries it alone. Observation, not a challenge: the row names psalm_device_inventory.json inside observed_substrate_signals - tool provenance rather than a strategy-file citation, so outside the register purge as written.

challenges.claim: The row's principal Hebrew citation, the full-verse run cited to oshb:Ps.150.6, is not quotation-grade: it collates at nfd rather than byte because its combining marks have been canonically reordered away from the source bytes.
challenges.evidence: collate.py --json run from a batch file (no shell transit of pointed text) over the two Hebrew runs of the rationale returns tier byte for the run cited to oshb:Ps.150.1 and tier nfd for the run cited to oshb:Ps.150.6. nfd is not quotation-grade: TOOLKIT.md states that only byte tier is quotation-grade for pointed text and that nfd means the bytes must be re-spliced from source via normalize_hebrew_in_json.py --write. The run carries the right 6 tokens but 3 of them have transposed combining marks - token 0 source=[U+05DB U+05BC U+05B9 U+05A3 U+05DC] row=[U+05DB U+05B9 U+05BC U+05A3 U+05DC]; token 1 source=[U+05D4 U+05B7 U+05AD U+05E0 U+05BC U+05B0 U+05E9 U+05C1 U+05B8 U+05DE U+05B8 U+05D4] row=[U+05D4 U+05B7 U+05AD U+05E0 U+05B0 U+05BC U+05E9 U+05B8 U+05C1 U+05DE U+05B8 U+05D4]; token 2 source=[U+05EA U+05BC U+05B0 U+05D4 U+05B7 U+05DC U+05BC U+05B5 U+05A5 U+05DC] row=[U+05EA U+05B0 U+05BC U+05D4 U+05B7 U+05DC U+05B5 U+05BC U+05A5 U+05DC] - that is 5 mark transpositions in which dagesh U+05BC and shin-dot U+05C1 have been moved AFTER the vowel into canonical NFD order (combining classes 21 and 24 sorted behind 10 and 18), erasing the source's point-first ordering. The byte-true source text of MT 150:6, spliced from verse_map_oshb.json and re-collated at byte tier, is כֹּ֣ל הַ֭נְּשָׁמָה תְּהַלֵּ֥ל יָ֗הּ הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ (oshb:Ps.150.6). That the oshb:Ps.150.1 run in the same field is byte-true localises the fault to this one run and matches the recorded copy-degradation signature (a display copy or an in-draft re-copy, not a source problem). Repair is mechanical: re-splice from verse_map_oshb.json and re-collate. Note for the toolkit rather than the row: citation_sweep.py passed this row GREEN because its Hebrew-binding arm accepts tier in (byte, nfd) for pointed runs, which contradicts its own docstring requirement that pointed quotes must reach byte tier.

challenges.claim: The row's register claim of no jussive, infinitival, or nominal-clause shift across the span, restated as the same imperative frame throughout, is false at MT 150:6, whose main-clause verb is a Piel prefix-conjugation form and not an imperative - a contradiction the row's own count of 12 imperative tokens already encodes.
challenges.evidence: Pointed bytes of the verse the row itself quotes. MT 150:6 token 2, spliced byte-true from verse_map_oshb.json, is תְּהַלֵּ֥ל (oshb:Ps.150.6), codepoints U+05EA U+05BC U+05B0 U+05D4 U+05B7 U+05DC U+05BC U+05B5 U+05A5 U+05DC: a taw preformative U+05EA carrying dagesh U+05BC and sheva U+05B0, then he with patah, then lamed with dagesh forte U+05BC and tsere - a Piel PREFIX-conjugation form, third person, agreeing with the feminine nominal subject of its own clause. Contrast the imperative shape carried by all 12 counted tokens, e.g. MT 150:6 token 4 הַֽלְלוּ (oshb:Ps.150.6), codepoints U+05D4 U+05B7 U+05BD U+05DC U+05B0 U+05DC U+05D5 U+05BC, and MT 150:5 token 0 הַֽלְל֥וּהוּ (oshb:Ps.150.5), codepoints U+05D4 U+05B7 U+05BD U+05DC U+05B0 U+05DC U+05A5 U+05D5 U+05BC U+05D4 U+05D5 U+05BC: he plus patah with no preformative and a waw-shuruq plural ending. Whether that prefix form is parsed as jussive or as plain yiqtol - the two are formally identical in the Piel of a geminate root, so no parsing choice rescues the claim - it is not an imperative, so both of the row's formulations fail at MT 150:6. Both witnesses render it non-imperatively: WEB has “Let everything that has breath praise Yah! Praise Yah!” (web:Ps.150.6) against the imperatives “Praise him with loud cymbals! Praise him with resounding cymbals!” (web:Ps.150.5). The row also contradicts itself within one field: a token scan of MT Ps.150.1-150.6 finds 13 hll-root tokens but only 12 hallelu-initial ones (3/2/2/2/2/1 by verse), MT 150:6 carrying two hll-root tokens at indices 2 and 4 of which only index 4 is counted - so the row's own figure of 12 already excludes this form precisely because it is not an imperative. check_universals.py returns 2 flags on this row, at [0].rationale and [0].observed_substrate_signals[4], for exactly these two statements: universals with no digit-bearing sweep beside them. The staged extract carries no morphology layer, so this is argued from the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings, which is the re-derivable path the toolkit prescribes for form claims.

challenges.claim: Quote/gloss span desync at oshb:Ps.150.6: the Hebrew run covers all six tokens of the verse while the gloss set beside it covers only the first four, dropping the closing hallelu-Yah that the row's own frame warrant depends on.
challenges.evidence: The Hebrew run cited to oshb:Ps.150.6 carries all 6 tokens of the verse - the byte-true source text, spliced from verse_map_oshb.json, is כֹּ֣ל הַ֭נְּשָׁמָה תְּהַלֵּ֥ל יָ֗הּ הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ (oshb:Ps.150.6) - while the gloss standing in apposition to it covers only tokens 0-3 and drops tokens 4-5, הַֽלְלוּ יָֽהּ (oshb:Ps.150.6). The dropped pair is the verse-final hallelu-Yah that psalm_device_inventory.json lists under halleluyah.verse_final for Ps.150.6, i.e. the exact element the row's frame warrant rests on. WEB renders the whole verse “Let everything that has breath praise Yah! Praise Yah!” (web:Ps.150.6), and that full rendering already stands earlier in the same field, so this is a truncation of the gloss rather than a misreading of WEB. Per the standing rule that a quote span and its gloss cover the same span, and per the parity rule that a repair re-cuts the gloss rather than shortening byte-true Hebrew, the fix is to extend the gloss to the quoted span. Severity low: no reader is misinformed about the verse's content. For contrast, the oshb:Ps.150.1 run הַ֥לְלוּ יָ֨הּ (oshb:Ps.150.1) is presented as the opener OF the verse whose WEB text follows rather than as a gloss pair, which is why it is not part of this challenge.
